problem: Most multi-hop datasets are extractive-answer datasets, so models can exploit heuristics or shortcuts instead of performing true multi-hop reasoning.
method: Semi-automated construction adding an extra question layer requiring one, two or all three of commonsense, arithmetic and symbolic reasoning on top of existing multi-hop questions; human verification of 1,118 samples; evaluation of five LLMs (Mistral 7B, Gemma 7B, Llama 3 8B/70B, GPT-4) with question-decomposition analysis.
key_assumptions: Extractive-answer multi-hop datasets let models use heuristics/shortcuts instead of true reasoning
Adding commonsense, arithmetic and symbolic reasoning layers on top of existing multi-hop questions produces a harder and more diagnostic benchmark
Perfect reasoning can be measured by whether all decomposed sub-questions are answered correctly
main_contribution: MoreHopQA, a generative-answer multi-hop dataset extending HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA and MuSiQue with commonsense, arithmetic and symbolic reasoning layers; plus an analysis of reasoning-step correctness showing only 38.7% (GPT-4) and 33.4% (Llama3-70B) of correctly answered questions have all sub-questions correct.
datasets: MoreHopQA (built by extending HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA and MuSiQue; 1,118 human-verified samples)
results: Abstract: models perform well on the initial multi-hop questions but struggle with the extended questions; only 38.7% of GPT-4 and 33.4% of Llama3-70B answers achieve perfect reasoning where all sub-questions are correct.
limitations: It is an evaluation benchmark, not a training method.
Small scale (1,118 samples), so fine-grained hop-depth stratification may be underpowered.
Abstract reports that no evaluated model achieves perfect reasoning, i.e. the benchmark is far from saturation, which is good for detecting transfer but bad for isolating small effects.
code_availability: Available: https://github.com/Alab-NII/morehopqa (evaluation code and data, per the abstract). Not independently inspected in this step.

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: Like 2WikiMultiHopQA this is a measurement resource. Its distinctive value to the idea is the sub-question-level correctness measure, which is a ready-made operationalization of 'does the model get the intermediate hop right?' — i.e. a candidate signal for the adaptive repair loop's one-hop failure detection.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.45: shared multi-hop QA evaluation with a focus on whether reasoning is genuine. Method overlap 0.1: benchmark construction, not training or supervision design. Evaluation overlap 0.55: sub-question decomposition and 'perfect reasoning' rate is conceptually the same diagnostic the idea needs for its one-hop-failure detection and deeper-hop transfer claims.
